title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from this and the neighbouring pages. X and Y are smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field k, with Albanese varieties A_X and A_Y and Albanese maps phi_X and phi_Y. S_X and S_Y are the summation maps from degree-0 zero-cycles to points of A_X and A_Y. B = A_X^* = Pic^0(A_X) is the dual abelian variety. Z is an algebraic correspondence between X and Y, considered up to numerical equivalence.

The previous page builds a canonical divisorial correspondence class c' in Cl(B x Y) out of Z (via the cycle Z'' on B x X x Y or B x A_X x Y). This class gives a homomorphism A_Y -> Pic^0_{B/k}. Cartier biduality identifies Pic^0_{B/k} = A_X^** with A_X, so c' defines a homomorphism of abelian varieties u_Z : A_Y -> A_X depending only on the numerical class of Z.

Corollary 1.3 is the functoriality statement: for every degree-0 divisor N on Y (a zero-cycle when Y is a curve) with the product defined, S_X(^tZ(N)) = u_Z(S_Y(N)) in A_X(k). Thus u_Z realises, at the level of Albanese varieties, the action of the correspondence on zero-cycles of degree 0.

Proof on this page:
- Biduality gives a bijection Theta : A_X(k) -> Pic^0(B), essentially a |-> class of the restriction of the Poincare bundle. So it suffices to check the equality after applying Theta.
- Lemma 1.4 (previous page) gives Theta(S_X(Z(N))) = c'(N).
- By the very definition of u_Z from c', c'(N) = Theta(u_Z(S_Y(N))).
- A first, more general formulation, Theta(u_Z(b)) = c'(b) for all b in A_Y(k), is crossed out. It is replaced by the version evaluated at S_Y(N).

Lemma 1.4 is reduced to Lemma 1.5. There is a divisor D, in the linear equivalence class of Theta on B x A_X (the Poincare divisor), such that with C = pi_*(Z''.(D x Y)) in Cyc^1(B x Y) one has D(phi_{X*}(^tZ(N))) = C(N) in Cyc^1(B), both sides being defined. This is a moving lemma plus the projection formula, dismissed on the next page as standard intersection theory.

The next page states Theorem 1.6: the l-adic compatibility a(gamma^n(Z)) o phi_X^* = phi_Y^* o u_Z^{(1)} on H^1 with Z_l coefficients. So the purpose of this section is the H^1 / Albanese part of the standard-conjecture programme. The action of a correspondence on H^1 is algebraic, comes from a homomorphism of abelian varieties, and depends only on the numerical class.
errors: Notation is inconsistent across pages and lines. Lemma 1.4 uses Z(N) while 1.3 and 1.5 use ^tZ(N). The map is written both theta and Theta, and the divisor both n and N.
The step 'A_X(k) -> Pic^0(B) is a bijection' uses Cartier biduality on k-points. This is fine over an algebraically closed k but is left implicit.
The crossed-out general identity Theta(u_Z(b)) = c'(b) for all b is in fact also true by definition (up to sign conventions). The correction only narrows it to what is needed, so it is not an error.
Lemma 1.5 (moving D so that all intersections are proper) is asserted without proof. It is standard (Weil/Chow moving), but the definedness hypotheses are delicate in positive characteristic.

ideas.what: A correspondence Z between X and Y induces a homomorphism of Albanese varieties A_Y -> A_X, constructed via a divisorial correspondence on B x Y and Cartier biduality, compatible with the summation maps on degree-0 cycles.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of Albanese/Picard varieties under correspondences (action of correspondences on Alb and Pic^0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (Variétés abéliennes et courbes algébriques, 1948), Matsusaka, Lang (Abelian Varieties, 1959)
ideas.where_published: Related material appears in Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968), which builds on Grothendieck's standard-conjecture programme

ideas.what: The induced homomorphism u_Z depends only on the numerical equivalence class of Z (Theorem 1.1).
ideas.modern_name: Numerical equivalence suffices for the action on H^1 / Albanese (the standard conjecture D is known in degree 1)

ideas.what: Reduction to checking equality in Pic^0(B), using the bijection A_X(k) -> Pic^0(A_X^*) from biduality, together with a moving lemma for the Poincare divisor.
ideas.modern_name: Biduality of abelian varieties / Poincaré bundle argument
ideas.where_published: FGA (Picard scheme exposés), referenced in this context

ideas.what: Compatibility of the action of the cycle class gamma^n(Z) on l-adic H^1 with the abelian-variety homomorphism u_Z (Theorem 1.6, next page).
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity of the H^1 part / Künneth component of correspondences via Albanese

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard verification of Albanese functoriality under correspondences, done via biduality and a moving lemma. It is classical (Weil–Lang–Matsusaka) and was absorbed into Kleiman's exposition of the standard conjectures. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 insertion should read 'sur A_X(k), car pour prouver' (the inserted words 'sur A_X(k)' and 'car' belong together above the line).

'grâce à la [-b-]dualité parfaite i.e. l'ensemblistes' should probably read 'grâce à la bidualité parfaite i.e. la bijection ensembliste déduite de A_X ≃ A_X^** = B^*'. The phrase 'déduite de' follows a struck-out 'A_X'.
The struck word after 'B^*,' is probably 'bijection' or similar.

Lemma 1.5: 'tel que, posant C = pi_*(Z''.(D x Y)) in Cyc^1(B x Y), on ait D(phi_{X*}(^tZ(N))) = C(N) dans Cyc^1(B) (et que les deux membres de cette égalité soient définis!)'. Here 'les' and 'soient' are crossed out and 'et que' is inserted, so the final reading is 'et que deux membres ... définis'.
